transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I’m here because my sleep has basically fallen apart. I’ll go to bed in my apartment and just lie there for hours, even with my laptop closed, mentally rechecking work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments… it just keeps going. And even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot during the day about many different parts of your life?

Yes, definitely. It’s like my mind keeps jumping from one thing to the next — whether I’m falling behind at work, whether I’m wasting money on school, whether my family thinks I can’t handle everything. Even small problems start to feel like they could mess up my whole future.
Did this all start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah, I think it really started when I began my evening graduate certificate program while still working full-time as an analyst. That was about a year and three months ago. Since then it’s just kind of been ongoing.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes. I’ll try to tell myself, okay, stop and just focus on one thing, but it doesn’t really work. One worry turns into the next, and then I’m checking my calendar, my budget, my assignments over and over instead of actually doing anything.
Do you often feel restless or on edge during the day?
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel tense a lot, like I can’t fully settle down, but I don’t always know if that’s what you mean by restless or on edge.
Aside from trouble sleeping, do you spend a lot of time worrying on most days?

Yes, definitely. Most days I spend a lot of time worrying. My mind jumps from, am I falling behind at work, to am I wasting money on school, to what my family will think if I can’t handle everything. Even small problems start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because of the worrying?

Yes. I’ll be looking at the same financial model or trying to read something for class, and I realize I’ve gone over the same paragraph five times and still don’t know what it said. My mind is already off thinking through everything that could go wrong.
Do you often notice your muscles feeling tense?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid that much attention to it, honestly. I know I feel tense in general, but I don’t know if my muscles specifically feel tight.
Have these worries and sleep problems been interfering with how you function at work or in school?

Yes. It’s been affecting both. I’ve started missing deadlines at work, which isn’t like me, and I’m falling behind in my certificate classes too. And honestly, I’ve stopped doing the things that usually help me stay grounded, like yoga, running, and cooking.
Do your worries feel mostly focused on the demands of balancing work and your graduate program?

Mostly, yes, but it doesn’t stay just on that. My mind jumps from, like, am I falling behind at work, to am I wasting money on school, to whether my family will think I can’t handle things. And then every small problem starts feeling like it could mess up my whole future.
Do you feel like you worry excessively about many different parts of your life, not just your workload and school?

Yes. It’s not just work or school. My mind keeps jumping to different things—like whether I’m falling behind, whether I’m wasting money on school, or whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. Even small issues start to feel like they could mess up my whole future.
If you were not dealing with the work-and-school situation, do you think you would still be worrying this much?

I think yes, honestly. Work and school are big triggers, but my worry doesn’t really stay there. It jumps to money, what my family thinks, whether I’m falling behind in life… and even small problems start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
Do you get tired easily during the day?

Yes. By the middle of the afternoon at work, I feel completely wiped out. Even basic things like answering emails or getting myself to the subway feel like they take a lot of effort. And resting on the weekend doesn’t really seem to recharge me.
Have you been more irritable than usual lately?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed being more irritable than usual, at least not clearly. I might get short sometimes, but I can’t say it’s been a big change.
Do you often feel keyed up or on edge?
I’m not totally sure what counts as keyed up. I do feel tense a lot, like I have a hard time fully relaxing, but I don’t know if I’d describe it exactly that way.
When you can’t fall asleep, is it usually because your mind is filled with worries?

Yes, usually. I’ll be in bed with my laptop closed, but my mind keeps going over work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments—just rechecking everything over and over. I can lie there for hours, and even when I do finally sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.
Do you ever have trouble falling asleep even when you are not worrying about anything?

Not really. Most of the time when I can’t fall asleep, it’s because my mind is still going—work deadlines, tuition, class stuff, just rechecking everything even after I’ve closed my laptop. I’ll lie there for hours, and if I do sleep, it doesn’t feel like I really shut off.
Do you get startled easily?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I get startled unusually easily, at least not that I’ve really noticed.
Do you often have trouble relaxing?

Yes, pretty often. I try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing, but then one worry turns into another. Before I know it I’m checking my calendar, my budget, my assignments over and over, and I’m not actually relaxing or getting anything done.
When you’re not trying to sleep, do you still find yourself worrying a lot on most days?

Yes. Even when I’m not trying to sleep, my mind jumps around a lot most days. I’ll go from worrying I’m falling behind at work, to whether school is a waste of money, to whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. And small problems don’t feel small to me — they start feeling like they could mess up my whole future.
